messages:
sara_sales: Heads up — Acme POC: embedded our console iframe in their admin app, but trace ids don't show up in logs (so correlation failing). They see 200 responses but no X-Trace-Id in their backend. Anyone seen this?

tj_se: Are they using our hosted dashboard or self-hosted/private? If private, an upstream proxy might strip headers. What's the request flow?

sara_sales: Private (Dedicated + on-prem forwarder). Flow: browser iframe -> their auth proxy -> our console iframe -> our ingest API -> log-drain -> Splunk. They pasted a screenshot of request headers.

matt_eng: Common culprit: intermediaries (nginx/istio) dropping non-standard headers. Also iframe SameSite issues can affect cookies but won't drop custom headers for curl tests. Can you get a HAR or curl showing header? Example curl:

  curl -v -H "X-Trace-Id: test123" "https://console.acme.example/_api/events"

sara_sales: They tried curl from their proxy host and header disappears before hitting our ingest endpoint.

tj_se: Ask them to check proxy config: proxy_pass and proxy_set_header — need to forward X-Trace-Id and X-Request-Id. For nginx add: 

  proxy_set_header X-Trace-Id $http_x_trace_id;
  proxy_set_header X-Request-Id $request_id;

Also ensure their proxy doesn't normalize header case or strip unknown headers in a transform.

matt_eng: Also check for any header-whitelist feature on their WAF. If curl from proxy host shows header missing, it's upstream. If they can tcpdump/ngrep between proxy and console it helps.

ingrid_sre_bot: alert: ingestion-gateway(acme-poc) returned 429s at 12:42 UTC (policy: default-burst). 12 spikes in the last 10m.

sara_sales: They also reported intermittent 429 spikes earlier in the day. Are these related?

tj_se: Possibly. If proxy retries remove trace headers or replay requests, our gateway will see many unique requests and hit burst caps. Two mitigation paths: have them set a stable X-Request-Id at the edge so retries dedupe, or we can bump their burst temporarily for the POC. Ops: @matt_eng can we add a short exception?

matt_eng: I can enable a temporary higher burst for acct-ACME-009. Need explicit account id and the window to open. I also recommend they set a stable request id at the edge (nginx $request_id or uuid) so we can correlate across retries.

sara_sales: Account id is acct-ACME-009. They updated nginx with the proxy_set_header lines and retested — header still missing when routed via their auth proxy (auth-proxy is a custom go service).

tj_se: If it's a custom proxy, double-check it doesn't rebuild requests from scratch. Look for code that uses http.NewRequest and forgets to copy req.Header. Also check if they inadvertently use http.Request.Clone without headers.

matt_eng: Also important: if browser iframe is cross-origin, response headers used by JS UI must be exposable. Make sure console responses include:

  Access-Control-Expose-Headers: X-Trace-Id

otherwise the frontend can't read the header even if it's present.

sara_sales: They ran tcpdump and discovered the header is present when requests go directly to our ingress, but when routed through auth-proxy it disappears. Auth-proxy team says they sanitize headers for security.

tj_se: Ask them to allow a safe whitelist of trace headers (X-Trace-Id, X-Request-Id, X-B3-TraceId). Provide them a short justification for the security team.

sara_sales: One more Q from the customer: does Dedicated POC include onboarding help for log-forwarder TLS mTLS and key rotation? And any short-term pricing for increased QPS during testing?

matt_eng: For POC we provide a short config assist session (30-60m) to validate forwarder settings (HEC tokens, TLS/mTLS). Key rotation cadence is configurable; for POC we can do manual rotation on demand. On pricing: sales can enable a temporary burst increase; finance handles billing adjustments after the POC.

sara_sales: Security team wants a one-liner: we support TLS + mutual TLS for on-prem HEC forwarders; keys can be rotated via support workflow. I'll pass that on.

ingrid_sre_bot: note: I applied a +2x burst exception for acct-ACME-009 until 2023-11-12T00:00Z (temp rule id: tmp-burst-374). Monitor for 429s.

sara_sales: After nginx change and proxy whitelist, trace id shows in our ingest logs — correlation fixed. UI still didn't display at first. They added Access-Control-Expose-Headers and now the console shows trace id in the top-right.

tj_se: Nice. Quick handoff checklist I can drop in the POC doc:
  1) Ensure proxy forwards X-Trace-Id and X-Request-Id (nginx snippet provided).
  2) If using custom proxy, copy req.Headers explicitly.
  3) Add Access-Control-Expose-Headers: X-Trace-Id on console responses.
  4) If using cookies in iframe, set Access-Control-Allow-Credentials and explicit origin.
  5) For log-drain to Splunk HEC, verify TLS/mTLS and token rotation plan.
  6) If 429s seen, check for retry loops and consider temporary burst increase.

sara_sales: Perfect, I'll paste that into the customer handoff and mark the POC ticket resolved. Thanks all :thumbsup: 

matt_eng: I'll create a short runbook and attach nginx snippets + a minimal tcpdump command for future debugging. Closing thread.
